$comment: Contract-conformance declarations. Every entry here is a declared-unconsumed
surface: a capability that exists, that no client reaches, and that is
deliberately left that way. It must match reality exactly -- a missing entry
is an undeclared finding and an entry that is no longer true is a stale one,
and both fail a -strict run. See docs/prds/contract-conformance-audit.md.

StateStoreService/ListCaptures.reason: Superseded by StreamCaptures. The remote adapter's ListCaptures method (staterpc/client.go) calls StreamCaptures, not this unary RPC, so no production client reaches it. The server keeps it implemented as a compatibility surface for callers of the raw proto.

StateStoreService/ListUndispatchedCaptur.reason: Superseded by StreamUndispatchedCaptures, on the same terms as ListCaptures: the remote adapter's ListUndispatchedCaptures calls the streaming variant, leaving this unary RPC reachable only through the raw proto.

blindSpots.reason: Extraction is textual, which is why this report is not gated. A path counts as a consumer only when it is the first argument of a call in code, so a bare constant, a dead array, an object property, or a commented-out call does not count; the calling function need not be named, so a rename is survivable. Limits: a path passed as any argument other than the first is not seen (accepting a comma would start crediting array elements); a request inside a template-literal interpolation is not seen; a path built from a bare /api fragment is reported as unparsable rather than silently contributing nothing; and a route is credited to every HTTP verb, so a route whose specific verb has no caller reads as consumed. Routes whose consumer is outside the dashboard (the asset mount, the health probes, the capture-intake webhook) are excluded from this surface by design: they have different consumers and are not part of the dashboard API contract.

Consumption is derived by scanning adapter bodies for calls through the generated client, so an RPC reached only through runtime-loaded code (Yaegi) or reflection would read as unconsumed. The scan also keys on the generated client field being named 'client'; renaming that field would report every RPC as unconsumed. No such path exists today.
